description: How networks are built and why they work: the layered models, IPv4 addressing and subnetting, the devices and cabling of a LAN, and the first steps in managing and securing one. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory networking course and the first half of the industry routing-and-switching certification.
modelledOn: Kurose and Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
Cisco CCNA 200-301 network fundamentals and access objectives
outcomes: Explain the OSI and TCP/IP models and place every common protocol and device at its layer.
Design IPv4 addressing plans with classless subnetting and VLSM and verify them by hand and with tools.
Build, cable and configure a small wired and wireless LAN with switches, a router and DHCP.
Explain how Ethernet, ARP, IP, TCP, UDP, DNS and HTTP cooperate to deliver a web page.
Detect and correct transmission errors with parity, CRC and checksums.
Monitor a network with ping, traceroute, Wireshark and SNMP and apply basic security controls.

units.title: Introduction to networking
topics: What a network is; hosts, links, switches, routers; LAN, MAN, WAN, PAN; topologies
Circuit switching versus packet switching; delay, loss, throughput, bandwidth-delay product
The Internet as a network of networks: ISPs, IXPs (including GIX in Accra), submarine cables
Network performance measurement with ping and iperf

units.title: OSI and TCP/IP models and protocols
topics: The seven OSI layers and the four TCP/IP layers; encapsulation and headers
Protocols, services and interfaces; the end-to-end principle
Application layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, FTP, SSH; sockets
Transport layer: TCP connection setup, reliability, flow and congestion control; UDP
Network layer: IP forwarding, routers and routing tables; ICMP
Following one HTTP request through every layer in Wireshark

units.title: IPv4 addressing and subnetting
topics: Binary and dotted decimal; classful history; private and public addresses; special addresses
Subnet masks, CIDR notation, network and broadcast addresses, usable hosts
Fixed-length and variable-length subnetting (VLSM); designing a plan for a campus
Supernetting and route summarisation
IPv6: address format, types, SLAAC, dual stack
ARP, DHCP and how a host gets on the network

units.title: Data link layer and Ethernet
topics: Framing, MAC addresses, Ethernet frame format
Shared media and CSMA/CD; full duplex; hubs versus switches
Switch learning, forwarding and flooding; the MAC table; spanning tree in brief
Link-layer tools: ipconfig, arp, switch show commands

units.title: Error detection and correction
topics: Bit errors and burst errors; Hamming distance
Parity, two-dimensional parity, Internet checksum
Cyclic redundancy check: polynomial division and hardware implementation
Forward error correction with Hamming codes; ARQ: stop-and-wait, go-back-N, selective repeat

units.title: Components and devices
topics: NICs, repeaters, hubs, bridges, switches (managed and unmanaged), routers, access points, firewalls
Layer-3 switches, modems, ONTs and the devices in a Ghanaian home or office connection
Reading device specifications: ports, speeds, PoE, throughput
Network diagrams and documentation

units.title: Cabling, wiring and wireless
topics: Twisted pair categories (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6a), T568A/B, straight-through and crossover; crimping and testing
Fibre optics: single-mode and multi-mode, connectors, attenuation; coaxial
Structured cabling: patch panels, racks, labelling, cable management
Wi-Fi standards (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax), channels, interference, site survey, mesh
Wireless security: WPA2, WPA3, enterprise authentication

units.title: Installation and configuration
topics: Configuring a switch and a router from the CLI: hostnames, interfaces, IP addresses, default gateway
Setting up DHCP and DNS forwarding on a small router; static addressing for servers and printers
Configuring a wireless access point; guest networks
Connectivity testing: ping, traceroute, nslookup, netstat; a fault-finding procedure

units.title: Network management
topics: Monitoring: SNMP, syslog, NetFlow; interface counters and utilisation graphs
Packet capture and analysis with Wireshark
Change management, backups of configurations, documentation, IP address management
Troubleshooting methodology layer by layer

units.title: Network security
topics: Threats: sniffing, spoofing, man-in-the-middle, denial of service, rogue DHCP
Access control: passwords, SSH instead of Telnet, port security, MAC filtering
Firewalls, NAT as a side effect, basic packet filtering
Security policies for a school or small business network

schedule.title: What a network is and how it performs
schedule.exercise: Draw the path of a message from a phone in Tamale to a web server abroad, naming each type of network and exchange it crosses, and compute transmission and propagation delay for a 1 MB file on a 10 Mbit/s link.

tasks.title: Build a star topology of one switch and four PCs in the simulator and verify with ping that every host reaches every other host
Send packets across a two-hop link with set bandwidth and delay, measure round-trip time with ping, and compare it against your calculated delay
Configure a bottleneck link between two LANs, transfer a test stream, and show how the bandwidth-delay product determines the data in flight

schedule.title: Layered models and application protocols
schedule.exercise: Draw a table mapping ten protocols to OSI and TCP/IP layers, and describe step by step how a browser request for a web page is encapsulated before it leaves the host.

tasks.title: Send one packet between two PCs in simulation mode and list the headers added at each layer as the packet is encapsulated
Set up a DNS server and a web server in the simulator, then resolve a name and fetch a page from a client and record the exchange
Diagnose a given network where a web page fails to load by locating whether DNS, the web service or the gateway is at fault

schedule.title: Transport and network layers in action
schedule.exercise: Write out the TCP three-way handshake and teardown for a request, then explain why UDP suits a voice call but TCP suits a bank transfer.

tasks.title: Capture a TCP connection in simulation mode and label the SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK packets with their sequence numbers
Configure static routes on two routers so three LANs communicate, then inspect the routing table on each router and verify with traceroute
Trace one HTTP request through DNS, ARP, TCP and HTTP in the packet trace, building a timeline of every layer's packets in order

schedule.title: IPv4 addressing and subnetting
schedule.exercise: For the address 172.16.45.200/21 compute network, broadcast, first and last host and number of usable hosts, then design a VLSM plan for a campus with four departments of different sizes.

tasks.title: Convert ten dotted-decimal addresses to binary and classify each as public, private or special using the base converter
Split 192.168.10.0/24 into four equal subnets, assign each to a LAN on a router, and prove with ping that hosts reach the gateway
Create a VLSM plan for departments needing 100, 50, 25 and 10 hosts from 10.10.0.0/24, implement it on routers, and verify connectivity

schedule.title: Summarisation, IPv6 and host configuration
schedule.exercise: Summarise eight contiguous /24 networks into one route and show the working, write three IPv6 address forms in compressed notation, and describe the DHCP DORA exchange.

tasks.title: Configure a DHCP server in the simulator, set one PC to automatic addressing, and record the address, mask, gateway and DNS it receives
Assign IPv6 addresses to two routers and three PCs, enable dual stack on one LAN, and verify reachability with IPv6 ping
Summarise four branch networks into one advertised route on the head-office router and prove that traffic still reaches every branch

schedule.title: Data link layer and Ethernet switching
schedule.exercise: Draw an Ethernet frame with field sizes, then walk through how a switch with an empty MAC table learns addresses over four frames, showing the table after each one.

tasks.title: Inspect one frame between two PCs in simulation mode and identify its source MAC, destination MAC and EtherType fields
Send traffic across a three-switch topology and record how the MAC address table on each switch fills, using the show command
Build a looped switch topology, observe the broadcast storm, then enable spanning tree and identify the root bridge and blocked port

schedule.title: Error detection and correction
schedule.exercise: Compute the CRC for a 10-bit message with a given generator by polynomial division, then encode and correct a single-bit error in a Hamming (7,4) codeword.

tasks.title: Write a program that adds even parity to an 8-bit value and detects a single flipped bit in 10 test cases
Implement CRC-8 division for a given generator polynomial and verify it detects all single-bit and a chosen burst error in a test message
Simulate a stop-and-wait and a go-back-N sender over a lossy link and compare throughput for 10 percent packet loss and window size 4

schedule.title: Network devices and documentation
schedule.exercise: Compare a managed switch, router and access point from three real product datasheets on ports, speed, PoE and throughput, and recommend a set of devices for a 30-seat school computer lab.

tasks.title: Place a hub, a switch and a router in the simulator, connect PCs, and observe how each handles a frame in simulation mode
Model a Ghanaian home connection with ONT, router and Wi-Fi access point, and verify two phones and a laptop reach an external server
Document a given 12-device office network as a labelled diagram with IP plan, VLANs and cable types, then check it against the real simulator topology

schedule.title: Cabling and structured wiring
schedule.exercise: Prepare a cabling bill of materials for a 24-port office rack with patch panel, giving cable category, lengths, connectors and labels, and justify fibre for the backbone.

tasks.title: Wire an RJ45 plug to the T568B standard in the hardware bench and verify all eight pins with the cable tester
Pick the correct straight-through or crossover cable for six device pairs in the simulator and confirm each link comes up
Design a two-building campus link choosing single-mode or multi-mode fibre for a 2 km run, and justify with an attenuation budget

schedule.title: Wi-Fi standards and wireless security
schedule.exercise: Run a paper site survey of a two-storey building plan, choose non-overlapping channels for four access points, and explain why WPA3 improves on WPA2.

tasks.title: Add a wireless access point and two laptops in the simulator, set the SSID and channel, and confirm both laptops associate and ping
Configure WPA2 with a passphrase on an access point and show that a client with the wrong key fails to connect
Place three access points on channels 1, 6 and 11 in a floor plan, reduce overlap interference, and verify roaming between them

schedule.title: Device configuration and connectivity testing
schedule.exercise: Write the full CLI command list to configure a small-office router and switch, including hostnames, interface addresses, gateway and DHCP pool, and a test plan to verify each step.

tasks.title: Use the CLI to set a hostname, IP address and default gateway on a router and switch, then ping between two connected PCs
Configure a DHCP pool with excluded static addresses and a DNS server on a router so clients get leases and resolve a name
Find and fix three injected faults (wrong mask, missing gateway, shut interface) in a given network using ping, traceroute and show commands

schedule.title: Monitoring and troubleshooting
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page layer-by-layer troubleshooting checklist for a school whose users say the internet is slow, and describe which monitoring data you would look at first.

tasks.title: Capture ping and DNS traffic in simulation mode, filter by protocol, and note the source, destination and type of each packet
Enable syslog and SNMP on a router, generate traffic and a link failure, and read the log messages and interface counters
Troubleshoot a given multi-LAN network with three hidden faults at different layers, recording your method and each fix with before and after tests

schedule.title: Network security basics
schedule.exercise: Draft a one-page network security policy for a small business, covering passwords, remote access, wireless, guest access and backups, with a justification for each rule.

tasks.title: Replace Telnet with SSH on a router in the simulator, set a local user, and confirm a PC connects only through SSH
Enable port security on a switch to allow one MAC per port, then connect a rogue PC and show the port shuts down
Write an access list that lets staff browse the web but blocks guest LAN access to the server subnet, and verify with test pings
